questions.question: Which type of unemployment is caused by a decline in aggregate demand during economic downturns?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cyclical**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclical unemployment** refers to the component of overall unemployment that results directly from cycles of **economic upturn** and **downturn**.
 
• It occurs when there is a significant decline in **aggregate demand** (the total demand for goods and services in an economy) during a **recession** or **depression**.
 
• When consumer spending falls, businesses experience reduced revenues and are forced to scale back **production**, leading to **layoffs** and a reduction in the workforce to manage costs.
 
• This type of unemployment is typically **involuntary** and is highly sensitive to the **macroeconomic** health of a country; it increases when **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** declines and decreases during periods of **economic expansion**.
 
• Economists use the **Okuns Law** to describe the relationship between **cyclical unemployment** and the gap between actual and potential **GDP** growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Unemployment**:

 
 
• Arises due to a fundamental **mismatch** between the skills workers possess and the skills required for available jobs.
 
• Often caused by **technological shifts** (automation), **globalization**, or changes in **consumer preferences** that render certain industries obsolete.
 
 
 
• **Voluntary Unemployment**:
 
 
• Occurs when an individual chooses not to work at the prevailing **market wage rate**.
 
• Reasons may include searching for a better job (**frictional**), pursuing education, or personal lifestyle choices.
 
 
 
• **Seasonal Unemployment**:
 
 
• Occurs when the demand for labor changes systematically according to the time of year.
 
• Commonly observed in sectors like **agriculture** (harvesting periods), **tourism** (holiday seasons), and **retail** (festival rushes).

questions.question: Article 22 provides safeguards to arrested or detained individuals under which two detention categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punitive and preventive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 22** of the **Indian Constitution** provides fundamental protections to individuals against **arbitrary arrest** and **detention**.
 
• The Constitution classifies detention into two broad categories: **Punitive detention** and **Preventive detention**.
 
• **Punitive detention** refers to the detention of a person after a **formal trial** and **conviction** in a court of law for an offense already committed by them.
 
• **Preventive detention** is the detention of a person without any trial or conviction, based solely on the apprehension that the person may commit an act that is prejudicial to the **security of the state** or **public order**.
 
• The objective of **preventive detention** is not to punish an individual for a past offense but to prevent them from committing an offense in the near future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Safeguards for Punitive Detention (Article 22(1) and (2))**:

 
 
• The right to be informed of the **grounds of arrest** as soon as possible.
 
• The right to consult and be defended by a **legal practitioner** of one's choice.
 
• The right to be produced before the nearest **Magistrate** within a period of **24 hours** (excluding travel time).
 
• No person can be detained in custody beyond **24 hours** without the authority of a **Magistrate**.
 
 
 
• **Safeguards for Preventive Detention (Article 22(4) to (7))**:
 
 
• A person cannot be detained for more than **three months** unless an **Advisory Board**, comprising persons qualified to be **High Court Judges**, finds sufficient cause for an extension.
 
• The **detaining authority** must communicate the grounds of detention to the detenu, though facts deemed against the **public interest** can be withheld.
 
• The individual must be given the earliest opportunity to make a **representation** against the detention order.
 
• Both **Parliament** and **State Legislatures** have the power to enact laws for preventive detention under the **Seventh Schedule**.

questions.question: Dharmapala, the Pala ruler, is credited with founding which of the following famous universities near Bhagalpur in Bihar?

__
 
• **Dharmapala**, the second ruler of the **Pala Dynasty**, established **Vikramashila University** during the late **8th century** or early **9th century** CE.
 
• The university was located at **Antichak** in the **Bhagalpur** district of **Bihar**, strategically positioned on the banks of the river **Ganges**.
 
• It was founded to serve as a premier center for **Vajrayana Buddhism** (Tantric Buddhism) and was intended to complement and eventually surpass the fame of **Nalanda University**.
 
• The institution was renowned for its academic excellence, housing over **100 teachers** and attracting thousands of students from across **Asia**, particularly **Tibet**.
 
• The university was presided over by highly learned monks known as **Dwara-Panditas** (Gate Scholars) who supervised the entrance examinations for prospective students.
 
• One of the most famous scholars associated with this university was **Atisa Dipankara**, who was instrumental in the reformation of **Buddhism** in **Tibet**.
 
• The site features a massive **Stupa** at the center and was eventually destroyed by the forces of **Bakhtiyar Khalji** around **1193 CE** during the **Turko-Afghan** invasions.

• Situated in **Saurashtra**, **Gujarat**, this university flourished under the patronage of the **Maitraka Dynasty** between **475 CE** and **775 CE**.
 
• It was a vital center for the **Hinayana** sect of **Buddhism** and was known for its courses in **Law**, **Economics**, and **Administration**.
 
 
 
• **Nalanda University**
 
 
• Founded in the **5th century CE** by **Kumaragupta I** of the **Gupta Dynasty** in present-day **Rajgir**, **Bihar**.
 
• It was the oldest residential university in the world, specializing in **Mahayana Buddhism** and drawing scholars like **Xuanzang** and **Yi Jing** from **China**.

questions.question: When fats react with sodium hydroxide to produce soap and glycerol, the reaction is classified as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saponification reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saponification** is the chemical process involving the **alkaline hydrolysis** of **esters**, specifically the **triglycerides** found in **fats** and **oils**.
 
• When **sodium hydroxide** (NaOH) reacts with these **fats**, it breaks the **ester bonds** through a nucleophilic attack by the **hydroxide ion**.
 
• The reaction results in the production of **glycerol** (a trihydric alcohol) and **sodium salts of long-chain fatty acids**, which are the primary constituents of **soap**.
 
• The general chemical equation for this transformation is: Triglyceride + 3NaOH rightarrow Glycerol + 3Soap .
 
• This reaction is **exothermic** in nature and is the fundamental process used in the industrial **manufacturing of soap**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precipitation reaction**

 
 
• Characterized by the formation of an **insoluble solid** (precipitate) when two **aqueous solutions** containing soluble salts are mixed.
 
• Commonly used in **qualitative inorganic analysis** to identify **cations** and **anions**.
 
 
 
• **Combustion reaction**
 
 
• An **oxidation** process where a substance reacts rapidly with **oxygen**, releasing energy in the form of **heat** and **light**.
 
• Typical products include **carbon dioxide** (CO₂) and **water** (H₂O) when **hydrocarbons** are burned.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation reaction**
 
 
• An **anaerobic** metabolic process that converts **sugars** into **ethanol**, **lactic acid**, or **gases**.
 
• It is mediated by **enzymes** or **microorganisms** like **yeast** and **bacteria**.

questions.question: Provision for “just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief” under the Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) is contained in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 42**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 42** of the **Indian Constitution** explicitly mandates that the State shall make provisions for securing **just and humane conditions of work** and for **maternity relief**.
 
• This article is categorized under the **Socialistic Principles** of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which aim to establish a **welfare state** and ensure social and economic justice for all citizens.
 
• The provision for **maternity relief** in this article serves as the constitutional foundation for various welfare legislations, most notably the **Maternity Benefit Act, 1961**, and its subsequent amendments, which provide paid leave and medical benefits to pregnant women.
 
• Under **Part IV** of the Constitution (covering **Articles 36 to 51**), these principles are considered **fundamental in the governance** of the country, although they are **non-justiciable**, meaning they cannot be directly enforced by any court.
 
• The phrase **just and humane conditions** requires the State to ensure that the working environment is safe, healthy, and respects the basic **human dignity** of the laborers, preventing exploitation and hazardous employment practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 41**:

 
 
• Directs the State to ensure the **right to work**, to **education**, and to **public assistance** in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement.
 
 
 
• **Article 43**:
 
 
• Focuses on securing a **living wage**, a decent standard of life, and full enjoyment of leisure for workers, while also promoting **cottage industries** on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Article 47**:
 
 
• States that it is the duty of the State to raise the **level of nutrition** and the **standard of living** of its people and to improve **public health**, including the prohibition of intoxicating drinks and drugs.
 
 
 
• **DPSP Context**:
 
 
• The **Directive Principles** were borrowed from the **Irish Constitution** and are often described by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** as the 'Novel Features' of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: Most of the route of the Orient Express (Trans-Continental Railway Route) majorly lies in which continent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Europe**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Orient Express** is a legendary **Trans-Continental Railway** service that began its journey in **1883**, connecting the western and eastern extremities of the **European** landmass.
 
• The original route was developed by the **Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits** (**CIWL**), a Belgian company founded by **Georges Nagelmackers**, aimed at providing high-end luxury travel across national borders.
 
• The primary journey connected **Paris**, **France**, to **Istanbul**, **Turkey**, traversing approximately **3,000 kilometers** almost entirely through **European** sovereign territories.
 
• Key stops along the historic route included major **European** cultural and political hubs such as **Strasbourg**, **Munich**, **Vienna**, **Budapest**, and **Bucharest**.
 
• A secondary popular branch, known as the **Simplon Orient Express**, operated via **Switzerland** and **Italy**, passing through the **Simplon Tunnel** to reach the **Balkan Peninsula**.
 
• While **Istanbul** is a transcontinental city, the **Sirkeci Terminal**, which served as the eastern terminus for the train, is located on the **European** side of the **Bosphorus**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asia**:

 
 
• Although **Istanbul** acts as the gateway to **Asia**, the **Orient Express** tracks did not historically extend into the **Asian** interior. Further travel into **Asia** required crossing the **Bosphorus** by ferry to connect with the **Hejaz Railway** or **Baghdad Railway**.
 
 
 
• **North America**:
 
 
• This continent is home to the **First Transcontinental Railroad** of the **United States**, completed in **1869** at **Promontory Summit**, and the **Canadian Pacific Railway**, which links the **Atlantic** and **Pacific** oceans.
 
 
 
• **South America**:
 
 
• Notable rail routes include the **Trans-Andean Railway**, which historically connected **Mendoza** in **Argentina** with **Los Andes** in **Chile**, crossing the high altitudes of the **Andes Mountains**.

questions.question: Which of the following executive powers is exercised by the President of India?

options.text: Deciding the tenure of the Governors
Appointing the Prime Minister and, on his advice, other Union Ministers
Appointing judges of High Courts and framing the rules of procedure of the Supreme Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Appointing the Prime Minister and, on his advice, other Union Ministers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 75** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Prime Minister** is appointed by the **President**, and other **Union Ministers** are appointed by the President based on the **recommendation** and **advice** of the Prime Minister.
 
• The **executive power** of the Union is formally vested in the **President** under **Article 53**, which states that these powers shall be exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him.
 
• As the formal head of the **Union Executive**, the President ensures the formation of the government by inviting the leader of the majority party or coalition in the **Lok Sabha** to serve as the **Prime Minister**.
 
• All **executive actions** of the **Government of India** are formally taken in the name of the President, as specified under **Article 77** of the Constitution.
 
• While the President is the **nominal executive** (de jure head), he acts on the **aid and advice** of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the Prime Minister, making the latter the **real executive** (de facto head).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conducting Elections**:

 
 
• The responsibility for the **superintendence, direction, and control** of elections to the **Parliament** and **State Legislatures** is vested in the **Election Commission of India** under **Article 324**, not the President.
 
 
 
• **Tenure of Governors**:
 
 
• Under **Article 156**, the **Governor** of a State holds office during the **pleasure of the President**. While the President can remove them at any time, the normal term is **five years**, and this power is exercised on the advice of the **Union Cabinet**.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Procedures**:
 
 
• While the President appoints judges of the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts** under **Article 124** and **Article 217**, the power to **frame rules of procedure** for the Supreme Court lies with the **Supreme Court** itself under **Article 145**, subject to the **approval** of the President.
 
 
 
• **Other Executive Appointments**:
 
 
• The President also appoints the **Attorney General of India**, the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**, the **Chief Election Commissioner**, and the **Chairman and members** of the **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**.

questions.question: Vasco Da Gama reached Kappad near Calicut on which date to establish trade relations with Indian rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 May 1498**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vasco da Gama**, a **Portuguese** explorer, was the first European to reach **India** via the **Atlantic Ocean**, completing the longest sea voyage of the time.
 
• He set sail from **Lisbon** on **8 July 1497** with a fleet of four ships, including the flagship **Sao Gabriel**.
 
• After rounding the **Cape of Good Hope** in **South Africa**, the fleet sailed across the **Indian Ocean** with the help of a local navigator.
 
• The expedition successfully reached **Kappad**, a beach situated about 16 kilometers from the city of **Calicut** (modern-day **Kozhikode**) in **Kerala**, on **20 May 1498**.
 
• His arrival marked the beginning of a direct **sea route** between **Europe** and **Asia**, effectively bypassing the **Silk Road** and the **Ottoman Empire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamorin of Calicut**:

 
 
• Upon arrival, **Vasco da Gama** was received by the local ruler, the **Zamorin** (Samoothiri).
 
• Although the **Zamorin** welcomed him, initial trade negotiations were difficult because the gifts provided by the **Portuguese** were considered insufficient by local standards.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Trade**:
 
 
• The discovery of this route led to the **Portuguese** dominance of the **Spice Trade** for nearly a century.
 
• It paved the way for future European colonization in **Asia**, particularly by the **Dutch**, **French**, and **British**.
 
 
 
• **Later Life**:
 
 
• **Vasco da Gama** returned to **India** twice more in **1502** and **1524**.
 
• He was appointed as the **Viceroy of India** in **1524** but died shortly after in **Cochin** due to malaria.

questions.question: The new classification system for economic activities in India termed National Industrial Classification 2025 (NIC-2025) was prepared by which national body?

options.text: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Industrial Classification (NIC)** is the essential framework for classifying various economic activities in India, ensuring uniformity in data collection across different **statistical surveys** and censuses.
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, specifically through the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, is the nodal national body responsible for preparing and revising this classification.
 
• **NIC-2025** was developed to replace the older **NIC-2008** version, reflecting the structural changes and modernization of the **Indian economy** over the last decade.
 
• A primary objective of **NIC-2025** is to synchronize Indian standards with the **International Standard Industrial Classification (ISIC) Revision 5**, maintained by the **United Nations Statistics Division**.
 
• This update is crucial for capturing emerging sectors such as **digital platforms**, **information technology-enabled services**, and **renewable energy** production, which were not fully detailed in previous versions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**:

 
 
• It manages the **Central Statistics Office (CSO)** and the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**, which are vital for measuring **GDP** and **inflation**.
 
• The ministry also oversees the implementation of the **Twenty Point Programme** and the **MP Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS)**.
 
 
 
• **National Statistical Commission (NSC)**:
 
 
• Formed in **2005** following the **Rangarajan Commission** report, it serves as an **advisory body** to improve the quality of official statistics in India.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**:
 
 
• Established on **January 1, 2015**, to replace the Planning Commission, it functions as a **policy think tank** focusing on **sustainable development goals** and **cooperative federalism**.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**:
 
 
• It is India's **central bank**, established in **1935**, primarily responsible for **monetary policy** and regulating the **banking sector**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the specialized kind of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in the production of haploid daughter cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meiosis** is a specialized type of **cell division** that reduces the **chromosome number** by half, specifically occurring in the **germ cells** of sexually reproducing organisms.
 
• It results in the transformation of a **diploid cell** (containing two sets of chromosomes, **2n**) into four **haploid daughter cells** (containing a single set of chromosomes, **n**), which are known as **gametes** (sperm and egg).
 
• The process involves two successive rounds of nuclear and cytoplasmic division, termed **Meiosis I** and **Meiosis II**, but includes only one cycle of **DNA replication** during the **S-phase** of interphase.
 
• In **Meiosis I**, homologous chromosomes pair up and exchange genetic material through a process called **crossing over** or **recombination** during **Prophase I**, which ensures **genetic diversity** in the offspring.
 
• **Meiosis II** is similar to mitosis, where **sister chromatids** are separated, eventually producing four genetically unique **haploid cells** that are essential for maintaining a constant chromosome number across generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitosis**:

• He formulated the famous **Drain of Wealth** theory, asserting that Britain was systematically siphoning off India's resources, capital, and wealth, which led to widespread famine and poverty.
 
• To quantify poverty, Naoroji used the **jail cost of living** as a proxy for the minimum subsistence level, arguing that even the diet provided to prisoners should be considered the baseline for survival.
 
• His calculations for the period **1867-68** suggested a poverty line ranging from **Rs 16 to Rs 35** per capita per year, based on the prices of essential commodities like rice, flour, dal, ghee, and salt.
 
• He arrived at this figure by calculating the food requirements of an adult and adjusting it for the total population, including children, through a weighted average method.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Methodology of Estimation**:

 
 
• Naoroji divided the population into two categories: **producers** (adults) and **non-producers** (children).
 
• He assumed children constituted **one-third** of the population and consumed very little, while the remaining **two-thirds** were adults who consumed the full **jail diet**.
 
• By taking the average of these groups, he derived the **subsistence level** required for a person to remain above the poverty line.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of Options**:
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**: Focused on the concept of **Gram Swaraj** and rural empowerment but did not formulate a statistical poverty line in a published book format like Naoroji.
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**: Chaired the **National Planning Committee** in **1938**, which later worked on defining basic minimum standards of living, but this was decades after Naoroji's initial work.
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore**: While he contributed significantly to rural reconstruction through **Sriniketan**, his work was primarily social and philosophical rather than statistical economic analysis.
 
 
 
• **Political Legacy**:
 
 
• Naoroji was a co-founder of the **Indian National Congress** and served as its President in **1886**, **1893**, and **1906**.
 
• He was also the first Indian to be elected as a member of the **British House of Commons**, representing the **Liberal Party**.

questions.question: In the context of Lok Adalats, which statement is correct?

options.text: Lawyers are mandatory in every case presented to Lok Adalat
Formal procedures and strict rules of evidence are followed
Proceedings are informal, flexible, and less technical
Only Supreme Court judges can preside over Lok Adalat sessions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Proceedings are informal, flexible, and less technical**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **Lok Adalat**, legal representation is not a strict necessity as the forum encourages parties to interact directly with the presiding officers to reach a compromise. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Lok Adalat** is not bound by the **Code of Civil Procedure, 1908** or the **Indian Evidence Act, 1872**, which allows it to bypass formal courtroom rigmarole and technical evidence rules. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The essence of a **People’s Court** lies in its **informal, flexible, and less technical** nature, which ensures that disputes are settled through a friendly dialogue and conciliation rather than adversarial litigation. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• While **Supreme Court** judges can preside, sessions are usually led by sitting or retired **judicial officers** of various ranks, including **District Judges** and **High Court** judges, assisted by social workers and advocates. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statutory Framework**:

 
 
• **Lok Adalats** have been given statutory status under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**.
 
• The award passed by a **Lok Adalat** is deemed to be a decree of a **Civil Court**.
 
 
 
• **Finality of Decision**:
 
 
• The decision made by the **Lok Adalat** is final and binding on all parties involved.
 
• There is no provision for an **appeal** against the award in any higher court, as the settlement is based on mutual consent.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction and Cost**:
 
 
• They handle both cases **pending** in courts and those at the **pre-litigation** stage, such as **marital disputes**, **land acquisition**, and **compoundable criminal offenses**.
 
• There is no **court fee** involved; if a case is already in court and then settled in **Lok Adalat**, the original court fee paid is refunded to the parties.

• The **Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE)** was established in **1947** and was historically one of the premier stock exchanges in Northern India.
 
• On **November 19, 2014**, the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** withdrew its recognition of the **Delhi Stock Exchange Ltd.**, marking its exit from the stock trading business.
 
• The **derecognition** occurred because the exchange failed to comply with the **Corporatization and Demutualization Scheme** and failed to achieve the mandatory **net worth** and **turnover** criteria required for continuous operation.
 
• Under the **Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956**, exchanges are required to maintain specific regulatory standards to protect investor interests; **DSE** was found non-compliant with these statutory requirements.
 
• Following its derecognition, the exchange was directed to provide an **exit option** to its shareholders and settle its administrative and financial liabilities.
 
• Consequently, the **Delhi Stock Exchange Ltd.**, which is the **fourth option** provided, is no longer a functional stock exchange in the country.

questions.question:

The correct answer is __**Multitasking and reliability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Multitasking** is the capability of a computer system, particularly a **Server**, to process multiple tasks or user requests concurrently. In a computer lab, the server utilizes **Time-Sharing** techniques to switch between login processes so rapidly that it appears to handle all students at the same time.
 
• **Reliability** refers to the ability of the hardware and **Operating System** to perform consistently without failure. Handling requests **without confusion** signifies that the system maintains high **accuracy** and **data integrity**, ensuring that student A is not logged into student B's account.
 
• The scenario highlights the **Multi-user** nature of server environments where the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** manages resource allocation across various network nodes efficiently.
 
• Servers are specifically designed with **Redundancy** and high **Fault Tolerance** to ensure that the influx of simultaneous data packets does not lead to a system crash or logic errors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• This relates to the ease of moving a computing device from one location to another. While **Laptops** and **Tablets** are highly portable, lab servers are typically stationary **Rack-mounted** systems.
 
 
 
• **Lack of memory**
 
 
• This is a technical limitation or a deficit. To handle many logins effectively, a server requires substantial **Random Access Memory (RAM)** and **Cache memory** to store temporary session data for every active user.

questions.question: The river Kosi frequently shifts its channel in the plains mainly because:

options.text: It traverses a long stretch of tectonic rifted lowland
It carries huge quantities of sediment from the Himalayas
Large upstream dams constantly modify their natural flow
Its flow is sustained only by seasonal monsoon rain

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It carries huge quantities of sediment from the Himalayas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kosi River**, an antecedent river originating in the high **Himalayas** (Tibet and Nepal), drains one of the most geologically unstable and erosion-prone mountain ranges in the world.
 
• Due to the steep mountain gradients and fragile lithology of its catchment area, the river carries an exceptionally high **sediment load** consisting of **silt**, **sand**, and **boulders**.
 
• When the river emerges from the foothills and enters the flat **Indo-Gangetic plains** of **North Bihar**, its flow **velocity** decreases drastically due to the sudden reduction in the slope.
 
• The reduced energy of the water makes it unable to transport the heavy debris, leading to massive **sedimentation** and the continuous rising of the riverbed, a process known as **aggradation**.
 
• As the riverbed becomes choked with silt, the river is forced to breach its natural levees and seek a new path with a lower elevation, resulting in frequent **lateral channel shifts** or **avulsions**.
 
• Historically, the Kosi has shifted its course westward by approximately **120 kilometers** over the last **250 years**, creating a massive **alluvial fan** known as the **Kosi Mega-fan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sorrow of Bihar**:

 
 
• The river is notorious for catastrophic **flooding** and unpredictable behavior, earning it the title **Sorrow of Bihar** because of the massive displacement of people and destruction of crops.
 
• Its major tributaries include the **Sun Kosi**, **Arun**, and **Tamur**, which join at the **Triveni** in Nepal to form the **Saptakoshi**.
 
 
 
• **Tectonic and Climatic Factors**:
 
 
• Unlike the **Narmada** and **Tapi**, which flow through **tectonic rift valleys**, the Kosi flows over a deep **alluvial basin** where shifting is primarily a function of **siltation** rather than structural rifts.
 
• While the **Southwest Monsoon** provides nearly **80 percent** of the annual water discharge, the sediment dynamics remain the fundamental cause of the channel instability.
 
• The **Kosi Barrage** at **Birpur** was constructed to regulate flow and manage irrigation, but the high **siltation rates** continue to pose a major challenge to flood management infrastructure.
